bounded_slice.candidate: Candidate-set completeness commitment for protocol-fixed digest-order fork resolution under one omitted same-generation branch.
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Local deterministic symbolic replay only, extending p1-sa-596. True fork set S={D2a,D2b}, both generation=2 and predecessor_digest=D1; protocol tie-break is fixed before packaging as lexicographically smaller candidate digest. Assume D2a<D2b. D1/D2a/D2b/Cset are symbolic content digests, not computed cryptographic outputs. No public-source fetch, actual hash/signature computation, hosted coordinator, protected/manual execution, secret persistence, scheduler mutation or second semantic leaf.

candidate_set_commitment_model.canonical_manifest: M = domain_tag || generation || predecessor_digest || candidate_digest_algorithm_id || canonical_encoding_id || candidate_count || sorted(candidate_digests)
candidate_set_commitment_model.trust_boundary: Cset must arrive through an independently trusted channel/state distinct from the mutable evidence package. The package supplies the full candidate list; the verifier reconstructs M, recomputes Cset, and only then applies the fixed tie-break.
candidate_set_commitment_model.minimum_result: For exact deterministic replay of the protocol decision rather than merely the final head, one independently trusted content-binding commitment to the complete canonical candidate-set manifest is operationally sufficient in this symbolic scope. A bare boolean 'complete' is insufficient unless it is itself bound to this exact package/set. candidate_count need not be a separately trusted datum when it is canonically encoded inside M; it is protected by Cset.

omission_matrix.reason: The verifier has both the complete committed input set and the protocol-fixed total order, so the fork choice is replayable without a dynamic selected-head datum.

Without completeness binding, deterministic ordering over an incomplete set can deterministically select the wrong branch. Trusted Cset turns the omission into an observable mismatch before selection.
The apparent winner happens to match the full-set winner, but the package still fails to prove the complete decision input. Outcome coincidence is not package completeness.
A total order makes selection deterministic only relative to the presented set; it does not establish that the presented set is complete.

omission_matrix.result: pass for final-head replay; not a pass for complete tie-break audit
omission_matrix.reason: The trusted head digest directly supplies the branch-choice fact and therefore tolerates omission of non-selected competitors when the required outcome is only the selected head. It does not prove that the protocol considered every same-generation candidate.

comparison.trusted_selected_head_digest: One independently trusted content-bound digest is sufficient and simpler when the useful outcome is only deterministic replay of the selected head. It authenticates branch choice but not candidate-set completeness or faithful recomputation of the tie-break.
comparison.trusted_candidate_set_commitment: One independently trusted content-bound digest over a canonical complete candidate-set manifest is sufficient for deterministic recomputation of the fixed tie-break, provided the package reveals all committed candidates. It is stronger evidence for decision replay because any omitted branch causes commitment mismatch.
comparison.information_boundary: Both routes can use one fixed-length trusted digest in this symbolic model, but they certify different propositions: selected_head_digest certifies the result; Cset certifies the complete decision input from which a fixed policy derives the result.
comparison.minimum_completeness_commitment: A content-binding commitment to the exact complete candidate set plus generation/predecessor/protocol-domain context. Per-candidate inclusion proofs alone do not prove absence of omitted candidates unless anchored to such an independently trusted complete-set commitment.

result.observation: Protocol-fixed digest ordering alone is not omission-safe. An omitted same-generation branch can change the apparent winner, and omission of a losing branch remains undetectable if only the winner is inspected.
result.inference: For replay that audits the decision procedure, the smallest practical independently trusted completeness primitive is a single content-binding digest of a canonical complete candidate-set manifest. For replay that only needs the final chosen head, a single independently trusted selected_head_digest is sufficient and semantically narrower.
result.package_completeness: pass only when all presented candidates reproduce the independently trusted Cset; otherwise reject. No claim is made that Cset distribution itself is solved.
result.replayability: pass for the exact symbolic complete-set package under trusted Cset plus fixed ordering; pass for final-head-only replay under trusted selected_head_digest; fixed ordering without either independent branch choice or complete-set commitment fails omission safety.
result.hidden_executor_absence: pass for this exact symbolic slice: local deterministic verification plus lightweight repository state/evidence transport only
result.quota_zero_assessment: The symbolic commitment/tie-break checks require no hosted runner, Codespaces, cloud compute/storage, paid API/model, artifact service or finite credit. Repository transport is used only for state/evidence persistence; rate-limit recovery remains cross-invocation.
result.conflict_check: CLEAN-safe: semantically consumed only current sanitized controls and own scientist_agents LATEST/p1-sa-596. No O-derived, downstream, other-worker, shared-ledger, protected-primary, manual-user or scheduler semantics were used.
result.uncertainty: Not tested or solved: cryptographic collision/preimage assumptions; actual digest/canonicalizer interoperability; independently trusted Cset or selected-head distribution; repository compromise; authorization; key distribution; rotation/revocation; equivocation by the trust source; multi-writer generation allocation; threshold fork choice; signed Git verification; large-set proof efficiency; or heterogeneous verifier cost.
